input.title: Corporate partnering: a strategy for high technology companies
input.abstract: This article is intended to provide directors and executives of emerging technology companies with an overview of the process of finding and negotiating partnering arrangements. Over the last few years we have noted an increasing number of our technology clients entering into long-term strategic alliances with other companies. These partnering arrangements have enabled our emerging clients to access new markets and to grow more rapdily. Our larger clients have used these partnering arrangements to access new technologies or to evaluate potential acquisition candidates with less risk. The key to successful corporate partnering is understanding your own strategic objectives and those of your potential partners and structuring the type of arrangement most likely to attain those objectives. What follows provides a framework for analyzing the technology company and its potential partners, outlining the steps required for successful partnering. The article is divided into four sections with the last two to be featured in the next issue of CLSR. The first section provides an introduction to partnering and discusses when a company should consider venture capital or a partnering arrangement. The second section provides a step by step description of the partnering process. The third section of the study provides greater detail about each partnering building block, outlining the positions that the technology company and its potential partner are likely to take in negotiations. The fourth section addresses additional legal issues that arise in international transactions that are not addressed within section two above. © 1992.

output.reasoning: O artigo não atende aos critérios básicos de busca por palavras-chave do protocolo (métodos computacionais, lavagem de dinheiro ou crime organizado) nos campos de título, resumo ou palavras-chave dos autores.
